newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SELONDA-RIOPESCA GROUP POST HIGHER H1 PRETAX.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SELONDA-RIOPESCA GROUP POST HIGHER H1 PRETAX.

text.p: Greek aquaculture company Selonda said in a statement its first half pretax profit rose 14 percent year-on-year to 1.729 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 43 percent to 1.4 billion drachmas over the same period.

"Interim results vindicate the group's forecasts for 1997 made earlier this year," it said. "The management's decisions on operating matters in 1996 have yielded fruits earlier than initially expected."
Selonda had pretax profit of 1.6 billion drachmas in 1996 from 0.81 billion a year earlier.

The company said it would issue later in the year a statement for its two deals struck in May 1997 with Singapore's Technology Development Fund (TDF) but disclosed that fish farming investments in southeast Asia were already completed.
"Our investments in sea bass farming units in Singapore have been completed," Selonda said.

Selonda signed two deals with TDF to export know-how through a joint development company in southeast Asia and commence a pilot fish farming unit with an output capacity of 300 tonnes of tropical sea bass --lates calcarifer.

Subsidiary Riopesca , the largest hatchery in the Mediterranean, turned in a pretax profit growth of 25 percent in the first half of 1997 to 571 million drachmas on turnover growth of 79 percent to 1,821 million drachmas.
Riopesca forecast in February profit growth of 50 percent in 1997, with pretax earnings hitting 1.2 billion drachmas from 0.8 billion in 1996. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
